questions.stem: A transverse wave on a string is described by $y=0.06\sin(5\pi x-20\pi t+\pi/3)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in m and $t$ is in s. Which option gives its amplitude, wavelength and speed?
questions.solution:
Comparing with $y=A\sin(kx-\omega t+\phi)$ gives $A=0.06$ m, $k=5\pi$ rad m$^{-1}$ and $\omega=20\pi$ rad s$^{-1}$. 
$$\lambda=\frac{2\pi}{k}=0.40\text{ m},\qquad v=\frac{\omega}{k}=4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

questions.stem: A liquid of volume $1.5\times10^{-3}$ m$^3$ is heated through $20^\circ$C. If its coefficient of volume expansion is $4.0\times10^{-4}\ ^\circ$C$^{-1}$, what is the increase in its volume?
questions.solution:
The increase in volume is $[?]$
$$
\Delta V=V\beta\Delta T=(1.5\times10^{-3})(4.0\times10^{-4})(20)=1.2\times10^{-5}\text{ m}^3=12\text{ mL}.
$$

questions.stem: The root mean square (rms) speeds of oxygen gas (molar mass 32 g mol^-1) and hydrogen gas (molar mass 2 g mol^-1) at the same temperature are v_O2 and v_H2 respectively. What is the ratio v_O2 : v_H2?
questions.solution: At the same temperature, $v_{\rm rms}=\sqrt{3RT/M}$, so $v_{O_2}/v_{H_2}=\sqrt{M_{H_2}/M_{O_2}}$. $$\frac{v_{O_2}}{v_{H_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{32}}=\frac14$$ Hence, $v_{O_2}:v_{H_2}=1:4$.

questions.stem: For the octahedral complexes $[\text{FeF}_6]^{4-}$ and $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$, which comparison is correct?

options.text: $[\text{FeF}_6]^{4-}$ is high-spin and paramagnetic ($t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}$); $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ is low-spin and diamagnetic ($t_{2g}^{6}$).
$[\text{FeF}_6]^{4-}$ is low-spin and diamagnetic ($t_{2g}^{6}$); $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ is high-spin and paramagnetic ($t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}$).

questions.solution:
In both complexes, Fe is in the $+2$ oxidation state, so Fe$^{2+}$ is $d^6$. F$^-$ is a weak-field ligand, while CN$^-$ is a strong-field ligand.
$$[\text{FeF}_6]^{4-}:\ t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}\ (\text{high-spin, paramagnetic});\quad [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}:\ t_{2g}^{6}\ (\text{low-spin, diamagnetic})$$

questions.stem: The ether shown is heated with excess $\text{HI}$. Which products and cleavage pathway are expected?

options.text: Iodobenzene and 1-methylcyclohexanol; cleavage at the aryl–O bond by $\text{S}_\text{N}1$.
Phenol and 1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane; cleavage at the tertiary alkyl–O bond by $\text{S}_\text{N}2$.
Phenol and 1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane; cleavage at the tertiary alkyl–O bond by $\text{S}_\text{N}1$.
Phenol and 1-methylcyclohexanol; cleavage at the tertiary alkyl–O bond without iodide substitution.

questions.solution:
HI protonates the ether, then the tertiary alkyl–O bond cleaves to form a stable tertiary carbocation; the aryl–O bond remains intact.
$$\text{1-phenoxy-1-methylcyclohexane} + \text{HI} \rightarrow \text{phenol} + \text{1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane}$$
Iodide captures the carbocation by an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway.
